title: Parable: Invitation by the Explaining Master and Conduct of the Two Groups

questions.question: What does the speaker say the ruler wants people to do first?
questions.answer: He wants them to know who their ruler is and try to recognize him.

questions.question: How are the decorations in the palace meant to affect the people?
questions.answer: They are meant to make the people love the ruler by seeing and valuing his art.

questions.question: What should people do in return for the ruler’s artistic work?
questions.answer: They should admire it and try to become beloved to him.

questions.question: What do the gifts and blessings show about the ruler’s attitude toward the people?
questions.answer: They show that he cares for them and treats them with kindness.

questions.question: How should people respond to the ruler’s kindness shown through gifts?
questions.answer: They should love him by obeying him.

questions.question: What response is expected when people see the ruler’s mercy and compassion in the blessings?
questions.answer: They should thank him and show respect.

questions.question: Why does the ruler display signs of perfection and beauty in his works?
questions.answer: He wants people to notice his greatness and long to meet him and gain his pleasure.

questions.question: What does the special mark placed on each work show?
questions.answer: It shows that each thing belongs to him and comes from him alone.

questions.question: What belief about the ruler should people accept after seeing these marks?
questions.answer: They should accept that he is one, unique, and has no equal.

questions.question: After the teacher spoke, what happened to the people in the palace?
questions.answer: They split into two different groups.

questions.question: What good qualities did the first group have?
questions.answer: They had self-awareness, intelligence, and sound hearts.

questions.question: What did the first group understand when they looked at the palace?
questions.answer: They understood that the palace had an important purpose and was not made for useless play.

questions.question: Why did the first group go to the instructor?
questions.answer: They realized he had the answers to the palace’s secrets.

questions.question: How did the first group speak to the instructor?
questions.answer: They greeted him respectfully and asked him to explain what the ruler had taught him.

questions.question: How did the first group react to the instructor’s message?
questions.answer: They listened carefully, accepted it, and benefited from it.

questions.question: What did the first group do after accepting the message?
questions.answer: They behaved in the way the ruler wanted.

questions.question: What reward did the first group receive?
questions.answer: They were invited to another higher palace and were given lasting happiness.

questions.question: What was wrong with the second group before they even acted badly?
questions.answer: Their thinking was spoiled and their hearts were darkened.

questions.question: What distracted the second group from the deeper meaning of the palace?
questions.answer: They focused only on the tasty food and their selfish desires.

questions.question: How did the second group treat the teacher’s guidance?
questions.answer: They ignored it and refused to listen.

questions.question: What careless action did the second group take with the drinks?
questions.answer: They drank things that were meant for another purpose.

questions.question: What happened after the second group became drunk?
questions.answer: They shouted, disturbed others, and broke the ruler’s rules.

questions.question: What was the final outcome for the second group?
questions.answer: The ruler’s guards arrested them and threw them into a prison fit for their bad behavior.

questions.question: In the announcement, what is the main reason given for building and decorating the palace?
questions.answer: It is to help people know the ruler and understand his greatness.

questions.question: What does the beauty of the palace teach the people about their ruler?
questions.answer: It teaches that he has wonderful skill and deserves admiration.

questions.question: According to the speech, how can people seek the ruler’s love?
questions.answer: By valuing his works and showing appreciation for what he made.

questions.question: What does the ruler’s giving of blessings show besides power?
questions.answer: It shows love, mercy, and generosity.

questions.question: What is one difference between obeying and thanking in this passage?
questions.answer: Obeying is the response to his love, while thanking is the response to his kindness and mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest people should feel when they see the ruler’s beauty in his works?
questions.answer: They should want to see him and be close to him.

questions.question: Why are seals and marks mentioned on each work of art?
questions.answer: To prove that the works are his and that no one shares in his rule.

questions.question: What idea about uniqueness is taught through those signs?
questions.answer: The ruler is completely one of a kind and without any partner.

questions.question: What happened among the visitors after the instructor gave his message?
questions.answer: They separated into two groups with very different responses.

questions.question: Why did the first group realize the palace was not meaningless?
questions.answer: Because they saw its wonders and understood that something important was intended.

questions.question: What question shows the first group wanted deeper understanding?
questions.answer: They wanted to know the secret behind the palace and what it contained.

questions.question: How did the first group discover where to find the answers?
questions.answer: They heard the instructor speaking and understood that he held the key to the mysteries.

questions.question: What does the first group’s greeting and request show about their attitude?
questions.answer: It shows humility, respect, and eagerness to learn.

questions.question: What did the instructor do first when they came to him?
questions.answer: He repeated his message for them.

questions.question: What sequence of actions led the first group to success?
questions.answer: They listened, accepted the message, benefited from it, and acted on it.

questions.question: Why was the ruler pleased with the first group?
questions.answer: Because they showed proper behavior and good manners.

questions.question: What kind of reward did the ruler give the first group?
questions.answer: He gave them entrance to a higher special palace and lasting joy.

questions.question: What caused the second group to fail morally and spiritually?
questions.answer: Their selfish inner desires controlled them.

questions.question: In what way did the second group behave like animals?
questions.answer: They cared only about eating and satisfying themselves.

questions.question: How did the second group treat the signs of goodness and the words of guidance?
questions.answer: They ignored both the good qualities in the palace and the teacher’s warnings.

questions.question: Why was drinking the special liquid a serious mistake?
questions.answer: Because it was not made for ordinary drinking and they used it wrongly.

questions.question: How did their private wrongdoing become a public problem?
questions.answer: Their drunken shouting disturbed the other guests.

questions.question: What does their punishment show about the ruler’s judgment?
questions.answer: It shows that disrespect and rebellion bring a fitting punishment.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to in the instructor’s announcement?
questions.answer: The people who came to see the palace.

questions.question: What does the instructor say the ruler wants through the palace itself?
questions.answer: He wants to make himself known.

questions.question: What does the passage teach people to do when they see beautiful design and decoration?
questions.answer: They should recognize the ruler and admire his skill.

questions.question: How should people answer the ruler’s love shown through blessings?
questions.answer: They should obey him and love him.

questions.question: How should people answer the ruler’s compassion and kindness?
questions.answer: They should thank him respectfully.

questions.question: What is the purpose of showing works of perfection and great beauty?
questions.answer: To let people see something of the ruler’s excellence and desire closeness to him.

questions.question: What do the unique marks on each artwork prove?
questions.answer: They prove the works belong only to one ruler and come from his own making.

questions.question: What conclusion should the audience reach about the ruler after hearing this?
questions.answer: They should believe he is one, unmatched, and independent.

questions.question: What division took place among the visitors after the speech?
questions.answer: They became two groups.

questions.question: Which three qualities are praised in the first group?
questions.answer: Self-knowledge, intelligence, and upright hearts.

questions.question: What was the first group’s first reaction to the palace’s wonders?
questions.answer: They realized something very important was happening there.

questions.question: What showed that the first group did not stay at a shallow level?
questions.answer: They wanted to understand the hidden meaning and secret of the palace.

questions.question: Why did they see the instructor as necessary?
questions.answer: Because they understood that he could explain the mysteries properly.

questions.question: What did the first group ask the instructor to do?
questions.answer: They asked him to tell them what the ruler had made known to him.

questions.question: How did the first group benefit from the instructor?
questions.answer: They listened with care, accepted his teaching, and learned from it.

questions.question: What did their acceptance lead them to do?
questions.answer: It led them to live according to the ruler’s wishes.

questions.question: What happened because the ruler was pleased with them?
questions.answer: He welcomed them into a higher palace and granted them ongoing happiness.

questions.question: What two inner problems are named in the second group?
questions.answer: Corrupted minds and deadened hearts.

questions.question: What did the second group choose to notice in the palace?
questions.answer: Only the food and things that pleased their desires.

questions.question: How did the second group respond to instruction and warning?
questions.answer: They shut it out and would not pay attention.

questions.question: What poor behaviors followed their overeating and drinking?
questions.answer: They slept carelessly, got drunk, shouted loudly, and broke the rules.

questions.question: How did the second group affect the other guests?
questions.answer: They disturbed and upset them.

questions.question: What end matched the second group’s behavior?
questions.answer: They were seized by the guards and put in prison.

questions.question: What is one major lesson of the instructor’s speech about the ruler’s purpose?
questions.answer: The ruler wants the people to know him through what he has made.

questions.question: How do the palace’s ornaments serve as a message to the visitors?
questions.answer: They show the ruler’s artistry and invite the visitors to appreciate him.

questions.question: What should admiration of the ruler’s works lead to?
questions.answer: It should lead people to seek his love.

questions.question: What do the blessings reveal about the ruler’s relationship to the people?
questions.answer: They reveal love, kindness, and mercy.

questions.question: Which action is connected to thankfulness in the speech?
questions.answer: Showing respect through gratitude.

questions.question: Which action is connected to love in the speech?
questions.answer: Loving him through obedience.

questions.question: Why does the ruler show his excellent qualities in visible works?
questions.answer: So that people will notice his beauty and want nearness to him.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the ruler placing a distinct sign on every work?
questions.answer: It means every work belongs to him and points back to him alone.

questions.question: What should people understand about partners or equals to the ruler?
questions.answer: They should understand that he has none.

questions.question: What happened right after the teacher’s message to the crowd?
questions.answer: The crowd divided into two groups.

questions.question: What made the first group ready to understand the palace correctly?
questions.answer: They were thoughtful, aware of themselves, and had good hearts.

questions.question: What did the first group conclude about the palace instead of seeing it as entertainment?
questions.answer: They concluded it had a serious and meaningful purpose.

questions.question: What moved the first group from wonder to learning?
questions.answer: Their curiosity led them to seek the one who could explain the secrets.

questions.question: How did they know the instructor could help them?
questions.answer: They understood from his speech that he held the explanation they needed.

questions.question: What does the first group’s behavior toward the instructor teach about learning?
questions.answer: True learning needs respect, careful listening, and willingness to accept guidance.

questions.question: What was the result of the first group’s good conduct?
questions.answer: The ruler rewarded them with a higher home and permanent happiness.

questions.question: Why was that reward suitable for them?
questions.answer: Because they were obedient, well-mannered, and worthy guests.

questions.question: What ruled the second group when they entered the palace?
questions.answer: Their selfish desires ruled them.

questions.question: What did the second group ignore besides the teacher’s words?
questions.answer: They ignored the beauty and meanings in the palace.

questions.question: How does the passage show the second group lacked self-control?
questions.answer: They overate, drank wrongly, became drunk, and acted wildly.

questions.question: What social harm did the second group cause?
questions.answer: They ruined the peace for the other guests.

questions.question: In what way did they offend the ruler?
questions.answer: They behaved without manners against his rules.

questions.question: What final consequence came to them?
questions.answer: They were arrested and sent to a prison fitting their wrongdoing.

questions.question: What does the speech teach about why the palace exists?
questions.answer: It exists to help the people recognize the ruler and respond to him rightly.

questions.question: What are visitors supposed to learn from the ruler’s decorations and artwork?
questions.answer: They are supposed to learn that the ruler is worthy of love and admiration.

questions.question: What is the right human response to seeing skill and beauty in the palace?
questions.answer: To appreciate it and try to please the ruler.

questions.question: How do the gifts in the palace point to the ruler’s feelings toward the people?
questions.answer: They point to his love and care for them.

questions.question: What two responses are expected from people when they receive these blessings?
questions.answer: Obedience and thankfulness.

questions.question: What feeling should rise in people when they notice the ruler’s lofty beauty?
questions.answer: A strong desire to see him and gain his favor.

questions.question: Why does the ruler put identifying signs on every crafted thing?
questions.answer: To show that each one belongs to him and no one else shares his ownership.

questions.question: What truth about the ruler’s nature is emphasized by those signs?
questions.answer: He is one, unique, and beyond any equal.

questions.question: How many kinds of response did the visitors have after hearing the message?
questions.answer: They had two kinds of response.

questions.question: What inner strengths marked the first group?
questions.answer: Clear awareness, intelligence, and good-heartedness.

questions.question: What did the first group realize about the events in the palace?
questions.answer: They realized the whole setting had a serious meaning and purpose.

questions.question: What question pushed the first group to seek more than surface enjoyment?
questions.answer: They wanted to know the hidden explanation behind what they were seeing.

questions.question: How did they find the path to understanding?
questions.answer: They turned to the instructor whose words explained the mystery.

questions.question: What respectful action did they take before asking for knowledge?
questions.answer: They greeted the instructor with peace.

questions.question: What was their attitude while listening to the explanation?
questions.answer: They were careful, accepting, and ready to benefit.

questions.question: What did their learning produce in their actions?
questions.answer: It produced behavior that matched the ruler’s wishes.

questions.question: What was the reward for their response in both place and condition?
questions.answer: They were given a higher palace and made always happy.

questions.question: What inner damage did the second group already have?
questions.answer: Their minds were spoiled and their hearts had lost light.

questions.question: What limited view did the second group have of the palace?
questions.answer: They cared only about eating and enjoying themselves.

questions.question: How did they treat guidance from the instructor and his helpers?
questions.answer: They shut it out and refused to hear it.

questions.question: What chain of bad choices led them to punishment?
questions.answer: They overindulged, drank what they should not have, became drunk, shouted, and broke the rules.

questions.question: Why were the guards sent against them?
questions.answer: Because they acted with bad manners before the ruler’s order.

questions.question: What kind of prison was chosen for them?
questions.answer: One suitable for people with such shameless behavior.

questions.question: According to the instructor, what does the ruler want from the people through the palace?
questions.answer: He wants them to know him, love him, obey him, and thank him.

questions.question: How do the palace’s beauties help people know the ruler better?
questions.answer: They show his skill, excellence, and care.

questions.question: What should people do when they admire the ruler’s craftsmanship?
questions.answer: They should seek to be loved by him.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with the ruler’s love for the people?
questions.answer: The blessings and gifts he places before them.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with the ruler’s mercy and kindness?
questions.answer: The same blessings and gifts show his compassion and gentleness.

questions.question: What two acts are taught as proper responses to these blessings?
questions.answer: Obeying him and thanking him.

questions.question: Why does the ruler reveal signs of his perfection in the palace?
questions.answer: So the people will notice his beauty and want closeness and approval from him.

questions.question: What do the special signs on every artwork prove about ownership?
questions.answer: They prove every piece belongs to the ruler alone.

questions.question: What do those signs prove about the ruler’s status compared with others?
questions.answer: They prove he has no equal, rival, or partner.

questions.question: What major change happened among the audience after the speech?
questions.answer: They split into a good group and a bad group.

questions.question: Why was the first group able to grasp the palace’s true meaning?
questions.answer: Because they were thoughtful and had sound inner character.

questions.question: What did the first group refuse to believe about the palace?
questions.answer: They refused to believe it was pointless or just for play.

questions.question: What led them to the instructor?
questions.answer: Their desire to understand the secret of the palace led them to him.

questions.question: What does the first group’s request reveal about their view of the instructor?
questions.answer: They saw him as truthful, precise, and necessary.

questions.question: After hearing him, what three things did the first group do?
questions.answer: They listened carefully, accepted the teaching, and acted on it.

questions.question: What was the ruler’s response to their good manners?
questions.answer: He welcomed them into a higher palace.

questions.question: What lasting blessing was given along with that welcome?
questions.answer: They were made permanently happy.

questions.question: What defeated the second group when they entered the palace?
questions.answer: Their lower desires overcame them.

questions.question: What did the second group choose over reflection and guidance?
questions.answer: They chose food, pleasure, and careless enjoyment.

questions.question: How is their refusal to learn described in the passage?
questions.answer: They ignored the instructor’s guidance and the helpers’ warnings.

questions.question: What actions showed disrespect after they overindulged?
questions.answer: They slept carelessly, misused the drinks, got drunk, and shouted loudly.

questions.question: Who suffered from the second group’s behavior before the punishment came?
questions.answer: The other guests suffered because they were disturbed.

questions.question: What final result came to the second group because of their rebellion and bad manners?
questions.answer: They were arrested by the ruler’s guards and put into prison.
